1(a)(i).assumed: Acceleration is the gradient of a v–t graph, found with a large triangle.

1(a)(ii).assumed: Read impact speed from the graph; KE = ½mv² with grams converted to kilograms.

1(b)(i).assumed: Take 80% of the KE, then rearrange ½mv² for v.

1(b)(ii).assumed: Rebound velocity has opposite sign; deceleration is still g, so the line is parallel and reaches zero at t = v/g later.

1(b)(iii).assumed: Height is the area under the rising v–t line, or v²/2g.

1(c).assumed: Drag grows with speed so resultant force and acceleration fall; gradient decreases, lower impact speed, later landing.

2(a).assumed: Meanings of elastic, plastic, ductile, brittle, Young modulus and UTS, and how each appears on a stress–strain graph.

2(b).assumed: Estimate an adult's weight; share between three legs; area = force ÷ maximum stress.

3(a)(i).assumed: Vernier calipers or a micrometer suit a diameter of about 2.5 cm.

3(a)(ii).assumed: Mean of readings; absolute uncertainty is half the range.

3(a)(iii).assumed: Sphere volume 4/3πr³ with radius half the diameter in metres.

3(a)(iv).assumed: Density = mass/volume, quoted to the precision of the least precise data.

3(a)(v).assumed: Add percentage uncertainties; the diameter's is tripled because volume depends on d³.

3(b).assumed: Extension = loaded − unloaded length; force = weight mg; k = F/x.

3(c)(i).assumed: Spring tension from kx; in equilibrium upthrust = weight − spring tension.

3(c)(ii).assumed: Upthrust = ρVg for the displaced liquid; rearrange for ρ.

4(a)(i).assumed: Parallel identical resistors give R/n; series combinations add.

4(a)(ii).assumed: Series sections share p.d. in the ratio of their resistances (or I × R).

4(a)(iii).assumed: Current through one resistor = V/R; charge = It; unit coulomb.

4(b).assumed: Current splits equally in identical parallel branches; with n, A, e equal, drift velocity ∝ current.

4(c).assumed: Number density is free charge carriers per unit volume; metals ≫ semiconductors ≫ insulators; more carriers means better conduction.

5(a)(i).assumed: Amplitude is maximum displacement from equilibrium.

5(a)(ii).assumed: Wavelength is the distance between adjacent points in phase.

5(a)(iv).assumed: Intensity ∝ amplitude², so square the amplitude ratio.

5(b).assumed: Two speakers on one signal generator; microphone locates maxima; vary f; x ∝ 1/f; v from gradient using λ = ax/D; protect hearing.

6(a)(i).assumed: Threshold frequency is the minimum frequency of radiation that releases electrons from a surface.

6(a)(ii).assumed: Threshold frequency is the f-axis intercept of KEmax against f.

6(a)(iii).assumed: φ = h × threshold frequency, then divide by 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ for eV.

6(b).assumed: Electrons diffract through graphite giving rings; needs λ = h/p comparable to atomic spacing; speed changes ring size.
